title: Nearby-cycle comparison for a morphism through its closed image
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian, $f:X\to S$ proper, and let $F\subset S$ be a closed subscheme through which $f$ factors [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $f_F:X\to F$ for the factorization. Let $\Lambda$ be finite with an invertible integer annihilator on $S$ and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $P_r(f_F,K)$ implies $P_r(f,K)$ for every $r\in\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. The same implication holds for full $\Psi$-goodness [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2, pp. 7--8 (comparison of the strict-local tubes through the image). Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text:
Orgogozo's displayed Lemma 3.2.2 uses $\mathbf Z/n$ coefficients. Here we prove its closed-image argument directly for the stated finite commutative $\Lambda$. If $n\Lambda=0$, the map $\mathbf Z/n\to\Lambda$, $\bar k\mapsto k1_\Lambda$, is well defined and unital. Illusie, Theorem 1.6.1 and its following paragraph, explicitly extends Orgogozo's proof to these coefficient algebras. The module-valued tube formula used in Step 3 allows any commutative ring, and the sections comparison used in Step 6 allows any unital ring; thus neither step requires $\Lambda$ to be cyclic. The faithful exact forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) commutes with kernels and cokernels, hence with cohomology. A module whose underlying abelian sheaf is zero is zero, so this functor detects cone-cohomology vanishing. We use no assertion that it preserves injectives or derived direct images.

Fix arbitrary $B\to S$ and $u:B'\to B$. Put $E=F\times_SB$, $E'=F\times_SB'$, $Y=X\times_SB$, $Y'=X\times_SB'$, and $L=K|_Y$. The maps $E\hookrightarrow B$ and $E'\hookrightarrow B'$ are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Y=X\times_FE$ and $Y'=X\times_FE'$: a map to $X$ already has its map to $F$, so its compatibility over $S$ with a map to $B$ is exactly a map to $E$. These identifications preserve all projections. Exact inverse image in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] keeps $L$ and its further restrictions bounded below. No Noetherian hypothesis on $B$ or $B'$ will be used.

source.place: Sections 1.2--1.5, especially (1.2.3), (1.3.1)--(1.3.2), (1.4.3); Theorem 1.6.1 and the following coefficient-extension paragraph, printed pp. 6--9. The closed-image argument follows Orgogozo Lemma 3.2.2, printed pp. 7--8.

proof.text: For either closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$ above (that is, $E\hookrightarrow B$ or $E'\hookrightarrow B'$) and a geometric point $a$ of $Z$, [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] gives a canonical Cartesian identification $(j_Z,h):Z_{(a)}\xrightarrow{\sim}Z\times_WW_{(a)}$, where $h$ is the local map of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3) for $i$; it keeps the nilpotent structure of $Z$. These identifications use exactly the structural maps. A composite of two local maps of (3) is local, is compatible with the structural maps, and induces the composite of the residue inclusions of (2); so by the uniqueness in (3) the composite $Y_{(x)}\to E_{(a)}\to B_{(a)}$ is the local map for $Y\to B$. In the same way, the local maps $E'_{(a')}\to E_{(a)}$ and $B'_{(a')}\to B_{(a)}$ induced by $u$ commute with the two squares, since both composites $E'_{(a')}\to B_{(a)}$ are the local map for $E'\to B$. If $b\in E$, a chosen specialization $c:B_{(b)}\to B_{(a)}$ of $B$-schemes restricts to $E\times_BB_{(b)}\to E\times_BB_{(a)}$, i.e. to a morphism $E_{(b)}\to E_{(a)}$ of $E$-schemes, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. The specialization itself need not be local.

source.place: Tag 05WS, lemma-quotient-strict-henselization; scheme interpretation Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring (etale-cohomology.tex); functorial maps Tag 04GU.

proof.text:
Write $g:Y\to B$ and $g':Y'\to B'$. Choose an arbitrary oriented point $z'=(x',b',c')$ of $V_{g'}$, where $a'=g'(x')$ and $c':B'_{(b')}\to B'_{(a')}$ is the specialization. Write $(x,b,c)$ for its image in $V_g$ and $a=g(x)$. The points $a',a$ lie in $E',E$. By [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology], applied with second morphism the identity of the base, the source and target stalks of the ordinary comparison are canonically
$$R\Gamma(M,L|_M),\quad R\Gamma(M',L|_{M'}),\qquad M=Y_{(x)}\times_{B_{(a)}}B_{(b)},\quad M'=Y'_{(x')}\times_{B'_{(a')}}B'_{(b')}.$$
Here the maps from $M,M'$ to $Y,Y'$ are the natural ones. Pullback of a source complex to $z'$ is its pullback to the image point $z$, by composition of inverse images. The formula applies because the complexes are bounded below; it requires neither finite type nor Noetherian bases. The oriented points in [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] detect isomorphisms and vanishing of sheaves. Since their inverse images are exact, they commute with kernels, cokernels and hence cohomology, and take a cone to its termwise cone. It therefore suffices to prove the desired cone vanishing at these points.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 3.2.2 and its proof, printed pp. 7--8; universal version following the lemma. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: If $b'\notin E'$, then $b\notin E$, since $E'=E\times_BB'$. The structural morphism $B_{(b)}\to B$ maps its closed point to $b$, by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). Its inverse image of the open $B\setminus E$ thus contains the closed point of a local spectrum and is the whole spectrum: a principal open containing the maximal ideal is defined by a unit. Hence $E\times_BB_{(b)}$ is empty, as is $E'\times_{B'}B'_{(b')}$. As $Y_{(x)}$ maps to $E$ and $Y'_{(x')}$ to $E'$, the tube projections force $M=M'=\varnothing$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every module sheaf on the empty scheme has its unique section on the empty object, so its sections complex is zero, as are its derived sections. Thus the stalk comparison in this case is $0\to0$, with zero cone.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 3.2.2 and its proof, printed pp. 7--8; universal version following the lemma. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text:
If $b'\in E'$, then $b\in E$. Step 2 restricts $c'$ and $c$ to specializations in $E'$ and $E$, giving oriented points for $Y'\to E'$ and $Y\to E$. Put
$$N=Y_{(x)}\times_{E_{(a)}}E_{(b)},\qquad N'=Y'_{(x')}\times_{E'_{(a')}}E'_{(b')}.$$
The Cartesian identities of Step 2 give $E_{(a)}\times_{B_{(a)}}B_{(b)}\cong E_{(b)}$, and likewise on $B'$. Reassociating fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore gives $M\cong N$ and $M'\cong N'$. For clarity, a pair of maps to $Y_{(x)}$ and $B_{(b)}$ agreeing over $B_{(a)}$ determines its unique map to $E_{(b)}$, because the first already maps to $E_{(a)}$; forgetting that map is the inverse. The two constructions preserve the projections to $Y$ and commute with the induced map $M'\to M$, by uniqueness in that same universal property. This uses the scheme-theoretic closed subschemes, including their nilpotents.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 3.2.2 and its proof, printed pp. 7--8; universal version following the lemma. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: The identifications also identify the comparison arrows, not just their endpoints. Here is the formal check. The formula in [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology] is induced by restriction from pointed triple neighbourhoods to the tube. By [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], $\beta$ is the mate of the pullback square followed by the counit. Pasting with a pointed-neighbourhood restriction and then with the tube projection gives, by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(2), the unit-defined cohomology pullback along $m:M'\to M$. On sections this says: restrict a section from a triple to its inverse-image triple, then to $M'$, which equals restriction to $M$ followed by pullback along $m$, since the projection composites agree. The unit description of this derived pullback is [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](2); [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] makes that description valid after forgetting the constant $\Lambda$-action and preserves cohomology pullback. Applying the same check over $E'\to E$ gives pullback along $N'\to N$. The commuting projection squares in Step 5 identify these two scheme maps. Thus the cohomology comparison square commutes in every degree, and in the derived category before taking cohomology. This is an application of the cited mate identities to the specified maps, with no base-change invertibility being presumed.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 3.2.2 and its proof, printed pp. 7--8; universal version following the lemma. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Assume $P_r(f_F,K)$. Its definition [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data] applies to the preliminary base change $E\to F$ and then $E'\to E$. It says that the cone of this comparison for $Y\to E$ has zero cohomology in all degrees $i\le r$. At points with $b'\in E'$, Steps 5--6 identify the ambient stalk cone with that cone's stalk, so it too vanishes through degree $r$. At points outside $E'$ Step 4 gives a zero cone in every degree. Exactness and conservativity of [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] now give $H^i\operatorname{Cone}(\beta_{g,u,L})=0$ for every $i\le r$. Both $B\to S$ and $B'\to B$ were arbitrary, exactly the two quantifiers in $P_r(f,K)$. This proves the truncated implication for each integer $r$.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 3.2.2 and its proof, printed pp. 7--8; universal version following the lemma. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Finally assume full $\Psi$-goodness for $(f_F,K)$ as defined in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. For any $B'\to S$, apply Steps 1--6 with $B=S$, $E=F$ and $E'=F\times_SB'$. The comparison over $E'\to F$ is an isomorphism by that hypothesis. Hence the ambient comparison is an isomorphism at the points whose generization lies in $E'$, and it is $0\to0$ at all other points. Conservativity [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] makes it an isomorphism on $V_{f_{B'}}$. This holds for every $B'\to S$, so $(f,K)$ is $\Psi$-good. This argument uses full invertibility directly; it does not assume a uniform truncation bound or replace the universal quantifier by finite-type base changes.
